emma (sales): quick heads-up — NeoChain wants to start a POC next week. they asked for an API-level compatibility with CompetitorX, plus pricing and security Qs. can SEs help scope?
raj (solutions): happy to. do we have their example requests?
marta (prospect - NeoChain): pasted a minimal example from CompetitorX below. main ask: identical request/response shape so our devs can swap endpoints with minimal changes. also need SSO + a short security questionnaire answered.
marta (prospect - NeoChain): ```
POST https://api.competitorx.ai/v1/generate
{
  "model": "compx-large-v1",
  "prompt": "Summarize the following transaction log:",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "temperature": 0.3,
  "metadata": {"session_id": "abc123"}
}
```
raj (solutions): ok — two parallel tracks: 1) compat shim (translate their call shape to Redwood API) 2) evaluate prompt parity / output diffs.
liam (eng): we can ship a small compatibility wrapper we maintain in the POC repo. trivial mapping: their model -> a Redwood model alias, and forward metadata as `user_metadata`. the main risk is token accounting/response truncation differences.
emma (sales): budget question from NeoChain: are there any one-off costs for the shim or will this fall under normal usage billing?
raj (solutions): shim dev time is our cost; we should include a small professional services line if they want us to host/maintain it long-term. for the POC we can OSS the wrapper and bill only for inference usage.
marta (prospect - NeoChain): that works. they also asked about matching exact responses for QA automation — they run golden prompts and diff the outputs. latency needs to be <300ms p50 for short prompts.
liam (eng): <300ms p50 is feasible on Dedicated for short prompts. for hosted we can likely get to ~350ms depending on region and model. recommend Dedicated for production parity.
raj (solutions): to reduce output diffs we should: 1) pin model version 2) normalize tokenization differences 3) run an eval set and iterate prompts. also consider a quantization/profile that mirrors CompetitorX if they're using a similarly quantized model.
emma (sales): can you draft a quick eval plan and sample cost estimate? i'll include it in the quote.
raj (solutions): draft plan:
- ingest their 100 golden prompts
- run on Redwood model candidates (rwd-compat-1, rwd-heuristic-2)
- compute exact string diffs, BLEU/ROUGE, and a small human pass for hallucinations
- tune prompts (stop tokens, temperature->0.0/0.2)
- if parity fails, fall back to shim-level postprocessing to canonicalize minor whitespace/tokenization differences

estimated POC usage: 100 prompts x avg 150 tokens -> 15k tokens per model run. run 3 candidate models x 5 iterations = ~225k tokens. Hosted cost estimate ~$0.45 per 1k tokens (example) => ~$101. Dedicated quote: monthly reserved capacity starting at $Xk/month for required latency SLO. (tweak in formal quote)
kayla (security): on the questionnaire: they asked about data residency, SOC2, VPC/private deployment, KMS. short answers: SOC2 Type II — yes (we can provide bridge docs). VPC/Private deployments — yes via Redwood Private, supports customer-managed VPC and on-prem. KMS/HSM integrations — yes (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and self-managed HSM available). retention & logging: configurable per-tenant retention; we can sign data-handling addendum.
marta (prospect - NeoChain): perfect. one more tough ask: CompetitorX returns a `request_id` and sometimes `warnings`/`best_of` fields in the response. our QA harness expects those keys. can we preserve them?
liam (eng): we can surface a compatibility layer that inserts `request_id` (map from our internal trace id) and a `compat.warnings` array if any heuristics triggered. for best_of we can expose `generation_variants` field. small mismatch: our streaming chunking differs so some clients see different chunk boundaries — we'll document that.
raj (solutions): recommend we deliver: (A) an open-source shim repo with Node+Python examples (B) a hosted compatibility endpoint for NeoChain during POC (C) a short integration guide and compatibility table mapping CompetitorX fields -> Redwood fields.
emma (sales): sounds good. can someone drop a quick code snippet for the shim we can hand to their eng team?
liam (eng): sure — basic Node example: ```
// shim: translate competitorx request -> redwood API
const axios = require('axios');
app.post('/v1/generate', async (req, res) => {
  const body = req.body;
  const rwd = {
    model: body.model === 'compx-large-v1' ? 'rwd-compat-1' : 'rwd-default',
    input: body.prompt,
    max_tokens: body.max_tokens,
    temperature: body.temperature
  };
  const r = await axios.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', rwd, { headers: { 'Authorization': process.env.REDWOOD_KEY } });
  // map back response keys
  const out = { request_id: r.data.trace_id, text: r.data.output, warnings: r.data.warnings || [] };
  res.json(out);
});
```
raj (solutions): add a small normalization step for punctuation and tokenizer differences so diffs are less noisy.
emma (sales): great. i'll propose: POC duration 2 weeks, deliverables: shim repo + integration guide + eval report + costs. i'll ask legal to prepare an MSA addendum for data handling.
kayla (security): i'll jump on the questionnaire draft. can someone share their standard SOC2 report & pen test summary? (cc: @legal)
marta (prospect - NeoChain): thanks team — can we get initial pricing + eval plan by EOD tomorrow?
emma (sales): yes — raj & liam will sync then post updated numbers.
raj (solutions): noted — i'll run the 100 prompts overnight and post a short report tomorrow morning.
